extraction_method: chrome-devtools MCP: opened https://benchlm.ai in an isolated-context tab (isolatedContext=benchlm-rescrape-20260906), read __NEXT_DATA__ for the current buildId (bSnECWfL7h_rTg8fm2fMe - the 20260904 buildId sO7LcSOMOSP0YXfukxegt is stale), then fetched the site's own SSG data endpoints /_next/data/bSnECWfL7h_rTg8fm2fMe/{index,models,benchmarks,llm-pricing,llm-speed,frontier-ai-models,llm-price-performance}.json. Slugs for both benchmarks and models were harvested from /sitemap.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml..sitemap-17.xml (85,507 <loc> entries scanned across 18 child sitemaps), not from the /models listing page which undercounts the catalogue; then /_next/data/<buildId>/benchmarks/<slug>.json for all 410 benchmark slugs and /_next/data/<buildId>/models/<slug>.json for all 411 model slugs. All 828 endpoints were fetched in ONE evaluate_script call using the page's own fetch() behind a 12-way concurrency pool with one retry per URL, saved straight to disk via the filePath option; the only DOM read was __NEXT_DATA__.buildId. Every script began with a location.href guard that throws (not returns) on the wrong page, and the resulting file size on disk was checked after the save (8,842,498 bytes).
notes: No XHR/fetch data API exists beyond /api/market (unrelated market blurb, not captured). All leaderboard data ships in Next.js SSG payloads, saved verbatim in raw.json.

raw.json holds the untouched pageProps for every benchmark page, every model page and the index/models/benchmarks/pricing/speed/frontier/price-performance pages. Model-detail payloads still arrive nested under pageProps.pageData; they were unwrapped one level to keep raw.json's flat shape stable across days, and the keys comparisonLinks, faqs, visuals, seo, radar and peerPosition were dropped from them for file size. The homepage leaderboard was normalized to homepageData.leaderboard = {rows, categoryLabels, rankingMode}. Every other field is verbatim; no payload field present on 2026-09-04 was trimmed and no new payload field appeared today (key-set diff of the benchmark, model and index payloads against 20260904/raw.json is empty in both directions).

The homepage leaderboard still ships as tuple-encoded arrays (39 columns, no column names) inside pageProps.homepageData.leaderboard.rows. Column mapping re-verified today, unchanged from 20260904: [1]=model, [2]=slug, [3]=provider, [8]=contextWindow, [10]=inputPrice, [11]=outputPrice, [12]=blendedPrice, [13]=tokensPerSecond, [14]=latency seconds, [15]=Elo, [17]=release date (ISO), [26]=displayScore, [27]=full-precision overall score, [30]=category scores array in categoryLabels order Agentic, Coding, Reasoning, Multimodal & Grounded, Knowledge, Multilingual, Instruction Following, Math.

rank for per-benchmark records is the position in the leaderboard order the site publishes for that benchmark (no numeric rank field in the payload), same convention as prior days. Entries with a null score are skipped.

rank for Overall was computed by sorting the 232 scored models (row[26] non-null) by full-precision overall score (row[27]) descending; the score reported is the rounded displayScore (row[26]). Category and Elo ranks are likewise computed by sorting the rows with a non-null value at that column descending. Cross-checked against the model detail pages: rankings.overall.total is 232 today, and categoryEvidence totals of 151 (Agentic) and 181 (Knowledge) match the category row counts computed here.

Per-benchmark records take cost_usd from the model detail page's pricing.blendedPrice, context_window from pricing.contextWindow falling back to the benchmark row's own contextWindow, and date from the model detail page's model.releaseLabel. Overall / Category / Elo records take cost_usd, context_window and date from the homepage row columns [12], [8] and [17]. Fields are omitted (not fabricated as null or 0) when no source has a value.

Benchmark name collisions exist across slugs; source_url disambiguates (benchmark pages use https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/<pageSlug>; Overall records use https://benchlm.ai/models/<slug>; Category records use https://benchlm.ai/<categoryKey>; Elo records use https://benchlm.ai/).

No values were estimated or invented. Missing data is omitted. Zero fetch errors; all 410 benchmark and 411 model endpoints returned HTTP 200. As on prior days the select_page+evaluate_script pairs needed many retries (WRONG_PAGE aborts) because other agents were concurrently reselecting tabs in the same shared browser session; every retry was preceded by a location.href check that threw instead of fetching on the wrong site, and the one large all-endpoints-in-one-call fetch needed only a single clean race-free window.

This site mirrors other publishers' benchmarks rather than running its own evaluations. Treat its rows as corroboration and prefer the original source (Artificial Analysis, Vals, LiveBench, Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, etc.) where they disagree.

Two deliberate normalizer corrections, both affecting only per-benchmark records. (1) Date off-by-one fixed: the 20260904 run parsed model.releaseLabel through a timezone-aware Date and shifted every per-benchmark date back by one day ("Sep 1, 2026" -> 2026-08-31). Today releaseLabel is parsed as a naive calendar date, which now matches the site's own ISO release column row[17] for all 411 homepage models with zero mismatches. Overall/Category/Elo dates were always taken from row[17] and were never affected. (2) Deterministic ordering: per-benchmark records are emitted in sorted benchmark-slug order instead of the previous run's raw.json dict-key order, which was really the nondeterministic completion order of the concurrent fetch pool.

One field-level nit changed: 20260904 emitted "provider": null on 6 BullshitBench v2 rows whose creator is null. Those rows now omit the field, matching the documented omit-never-fabricate rule used everywhere else. No other field was added or removed. The record schema remains model, provider, benchmark, metric, score, rank, cost_usd, context_window, date, source_url, plus input_price_usd_per_mtok, output_price_usd_per_mtok, tokens_per_second and latency_ttft_s on Overall records.

Method note for the next run: the normalizer used today was validated by re-running it against 20260904/raw.json in a bug-compatible mode, which reproduced 20260904/normalized.json exactly except for the 6 provider-null rows described above.
